issues.failure_explanation: For p>1 the claimed inequality has no factor 2^{p-1} and is false. Take d=1, Lambda=Z, h=1, p=2, mu=delta_{0.51}. The cell containing 0.51 is centred at 1, so the left side is 1. The right side is 1/4+0.2601=0.5101. The proof breaks in three places. The lower bound |x| >= ||h lambda| - rad| fails when rad exceeds 2|h lambda|; only |x| >= |h lambda| - rad holds. The step from |x| >= |h lambda| - rad to |x|^p >= |h lambda|^p - rad^p uses (a-b)^p >= a^p-b^p, which is false for p>1 because t^p is superadditive. The factor mu(V_{h lambda}) is dropped from the left side when passing to the 'whereby' line and when summing. The correct estimate comes from |h lambda| <= |x| + h rad(V_0) and convexity, and carries a factor 2^{p-1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (i) by sum_lambda |h lambda|^p mu(V_{h lambda}) <= 2^{p-1}(M_p(mu) + h^p rad(V_0)^p), proved from |h lambda| <= |x| + h rad(V_0). Adjust the constants in the moment computations of Theorems 4.1 and 5.1.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed moment bounds in Theorem 4.1 (for mu_h) and Theorem 5.1 (for nu_h) are false as written for p>1. In the same example, int |x|^2 d mu_h = 1 > 0.5101. The qualitative claims mu_h, nu_h in W_p and the W_p rates are unaffected, since the coupling arguments do not use the lemma.
issues.title: Lemma 3.2(i) is false for p>1 (invalid lower bound and (a-b)^p >= a^p-b^p)
issues.why_classification: The fix is a short local replacement of a constant. Only finiteness of moments is needed downstream, and all rate claims survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The number of atoms of mu_h is the number of lattice cells V_{h lambda} that meet the support. The proof bounds this by N(B_R, hV_0), the minimal number of translates of hV_0 by arbitrary vectors needed to cover B_R. Lattice-aligned cells can need more than an optimal free covering, and no argument relates the two. A bound of the form 3^d N(B_R, hV_0) is the natural one, since each free translate meets at most 3^d lattice cells. Separately, the theorem allows every N, but h = 3(calN/N)^{1/d} exceeds 1 when N < 3^d calN. Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 4.1 are stated only for h in (0,1], and the inequality (1+2/h)^d <= 3^d h^{-d} fails for h>1. So the 'at most N terms' claim is unsupported as stated.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a lemma bounding the number of cells of h*Lambda meeting B_R by 3^d N(B_R, hV_0), and restrict to h<=1 (N >= 3^d calN) or treat h>1 separately. The step size then becomes h = 9 (calN/N)^{1/d} and the constants in the statement change from 3 to 9.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee of at most N terms with the explicit constant 3 rad(V_0) calN^{1/d} N^{-1/d} is not established, either for all N or for the lattice-cell count. Corollary 5.2 (which says to mimic this proof) and Corollary 6.2 inherit the same gap.
issues.title: N-term count in Theorem 4.2 conflates arbitrary-translate covering numbers with lattice cells and uses h<=1 results for h>1
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a new short counting lemma and a restriction on N. The rate O(N^{-1/d}) survives, but the stated explicit constants and the all-N scope change.

issues.failure_explanation: For general N the unit cube is not tiled by exactly N cubes of side N^{-1/d} (this needs N^{1/d} to be an integer). The lattice (N^{-1/d}Z)^d also contains the origin, so its cells are centred at multiples of h. Take d=1, N=2, so h=1/2, and mu uniform on (-1/2,1/2). The cells [-1/4,1/4), [1/4,3/4), [-3/4,-1/4) all carry mass, giving 3 atoms. For N=4, h=1/4 gives 5 atoms. Only odd integer N^{1/d} gives exactly N cells. The W_p bound (sqrt d/2) N^{-1/d} still follows from Theorem 4.1, but the 'at most N-term' claim fails.

failure_location.quote: Setting $h=N^{-\frac1d}$ yields $N$ cubes of length $N^{-\frac1d}$ in the unit cube

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use m=floor(N^{1/d}) cells per side (or the largest suitable integer), with the lattice shifted so the cube is tiled, and h=1/m <= 2N^{-1/d}. This yields at most N terms with constant about sqrt(d) in place of sqrt(d)/2 (and 2 sqrt(d) in place of sqrt(d) for Corollary 5.3).
issues.overall_effect: The 'at most N-term' guarantee with constant sqrt(d)/2 (and sqrt(d) for the piecewise-constant version in Corollary 5.3) is false for most N. The pixel/voxel camera interpretation relies on an exact N-cell count.
issues.title: Corollary 4.3: h=N^{-1/d} does not give at most N cells in the cube for the origin-centred lattice
issues.why_classification: A simple modification of h and a shift restore at most N terms with the same rate. The explicit constants and the specified lattice Lambda_N change, so this is a limited weakening rather than a typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The integral of r^{d-1}/r^{d+1} over r>=R equals 1/R, which is at most 1 only if R>=1. The theorem places no restriction on R. Counterexample: p=1, R=0.1, eps=0.05, mu_perp=mu_d=0, and f_mu equal to eps/(3C|x|^{d+2}) for |x|>R. This has mass 0.833, with the remaining mass 0.167 placed inside B_R under the same density bound. Radial projection onto the convex ball is optimal, so W_1(mu, mu_hat) equals int (|x|-R) d mu = eps/(3(p+1)R) = 0.083 > eps. Hypothesis 1 is satisfied but the conclusion W_p<eps fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume R>=1, or replace the density hypothesis by f_mu(x) <= eps^p R/(3C|x|^{p+d+1}) (or any constant making the radial integral at most 1), and rerun the same computation.
issues.overall_effect: The decay hypothesis on the absolutely continuous part does not imply W_p(mu, mu_hat)<eps for R<1/(p+1), and the proof is invalid for R<1. Corollary 6.2 uses this bound.
issues.title: Theorem 6.1: bound of I_1 requires R>=1 (integral of r^{-2} equals 1/R)
issues.why_classification: A local change of the hypothesis constant or an added condition R>=1 repairs the step. The method and conclusion are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The terms are 1/(delta+k)^2 for k>=0, with delta = floor(R)+1-R in (0,1]. The sum equals pi^2/6 only for delta=1 (integer R); for non-integer R it exceeds pi^2/6, and it blows up as R approaches an integer from below. Counterexample: p=1, R=0.6, eps=0.1. Put mass m_j = eps^p/(3(j+1-R)^{p+2}) * 6/pi^2 uniformly on the sphere of radius j+1 for each j>=0, which is singular continuous with total mass below 1 and satisfies hypothesis 2. Then I_2 = (eps^p/3)(6/pi^2) * sum_{k>=0} (k+0.4)^{-2}, approximately 1.47 eps^p. Hence W_p(mu, mu_hat)^p >= I_2 > eps^p, contradicting the conclusion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Index the shells from R, i.e. use B_{(R+k, R+k+1]} for k>=0 in hypothesis 2. The sum is then sum_{k>=1} k^{-2} = pi^2/6, and the rest of the I_2 estimate goes through.
issues.overall_effect: Hypothesis 2 does not control the cost of moving the singular continuous part to the ball for non-integer R, so the stated conclusion W_p(mu, mu_hat)<eps fails. Corollary 6.2's eps term is unsupported in that case.
issues.title: Theorem 6.1: shell-sum bound pi^2/6 holds only for integer R, so the singular-continuous condition does not give I_2<eps^p/3
issues.why_classification: Re-indexing the shells in the hypothesis and the corresponding sum is a short local repair. The rest of the argument stays the same.
